fatal_errors: The proposed Fe20Co20Ni20Mn20Cu20 coating, chloride electrolyte, 60 °C interrupted sliding, and oxidation-inhibited comparator do not reconstruct the AlCoCrFeNi2.1-versus-DS2205 thermal-shock and deionized-water comparison.

Chromium oxide is proposed as a regenerated film even though the stated Fe-Co-Ni-Mn-Cu alloy contains no chromium; any chromium signal could originate from the SS-304 substrate and would not establish HEA self-healing.
The cited evidence concerns oxide formation or heat treatment near 800 °C and does not demonstrate rapid passive-film regeneration during sliding at 60 °C.
The oxidation-inhibited baseline is insufficiently defined and would likely alter surface chemistry, corrosion susceptibility, or mechanical properties independently of film-regeneration kinetics.
explanation: The response identifies a broadly relevant depassivation–repassivation competition, which overlaps with one part of the target mechanism. It does not recover the key material system, dual-phase lamellar structural stability, DS2205 baseline, rapid 1100 °C thermal shocks, deionized-water test conditions, or the temperature-dependent transition from abrasion to minimum-wear polishing and then oxide/third-body wear. It also fails to predict the observed nonmonotonic minimum near 50 °C or the HEA's order-of-magnitude advantage over DS2205. The proposed experiment could test whether an oxide affects degradation, but chemical inhibition is a major confound and the measurements do not cleanly separate mechanical wear, corrosion, and their synergy. Prior evidence only indirectly supports protective oxides and cannot validate the claimed 60 °C cyclic self-healing kinetics.
